posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
It's actually unclear to me whether or not we are allowed to share the Easter Egg stuff we saw. 

It also feels a little weird talking about the Vengeance cards or box. We went to a release party, so it's released, but the Kickstarter rewards haven't been sent out yet. I'm pretty sure it is ok to talk about it. Just feels a little weird.

 

The party was fun. It was very informal. There was no schedule beyond start and stop times. it started off with people trickling in, picking up games, and in some cases introducing themselves to people they'd only ever interacted w/ online. Paul was often at a table helping people pick up their games or packing Kickstarter boxes, often with Jodie. Christiopher and Adam were circulating. There were half a dozen tables set up in the front of the warehouse that filled up with people playing Vengeance. There were also games going on everywhere they could be fit into the office area -- the conference room, an unused office, the front lobby, and a wide hallway.I'm pretty sure we had ten simultaneous games while also having other people socializing, so I'm guessing the attendance was round 50-60 people.

All the office spaces were open and people wandered in and out. Paul has an office with some beautiful Lord of the Rings art and weapons mounted on the wall. The spare office has a bookshelf filled with fantasy miniatures. Christopher and Adam share an office with their desks facing each other. On one end Adam had hung eight gorgeous, framed comic pages. It wasn't Sentinels. I didn't recognize it. I don't _think_ it was his art work, but am not sure. There was also a whiteboard in their shared office. It already had a large line drawing of Baron Blade on it. Adam drew Legacy on the other side, while I held up my laptop so the people who were interacting via G+ could see him in action.

Reckless showed up with his perler (sp?) ... uh ... artwork? (not sure how to describe these). These are individually great, but even more impressive as a collection. Evan and his friends were doing various film/interview things and Evan coralled the forumites for a photo. Who knows what I may have missed, as well. You certainly couldn't see everything that was going on from a single vantage point.

Towards five, Christopher announced it was time for dinner. Those who had the time and inclination (~30) regrouped at a nearby Indian restaurant for a tasty buffet. Our carload of people left before 7, perhaps a bit earlier than we might have otherwise, in order to try to outrun the freezing rain that was overtaking the area.

I spoke to people who'd traveled from Fayetteville, Kansas City, Chicago, Indianapolis, and Columbus. And Brocolli. Who's from Texas, but he flies enough that maybe it wasn't very onerous to take one more trip. I'm not sure where else people might have travelled from.

It was pretty low key, but quite nice.
